sources.title: Ripple ownership (document excerpt)
sources.text: 3. **Single synchronous owner.** Each HTTP handler completes all database calls without `await`. A transaction cannot overlap another handler. An asynchronous store implementation must add an explicit queue covering reads as well as the entire write transaction. Scaling beyond local single-user is not supported.

sources.title: Ripple atomicity (document excerpt)
sources.text: 7. **Changes are atomic and idempotent.** UUID requestId + payload fingerprint detects reuse. Within one explicit transaction, lookup prior request, check revision, validate evidence, query the old graph, save Change and Review snapshots, then update body/revision. A failure rolls the whole write back. No automatic retry on a conflicting revision.

sources.title: Ripple assets (document excerpt)
sources.text: 10. **Local server and assets.** API and UI share one loopback origin. Host and Origin checks reject cross-site writes; JSON schema/body limits reject malformed input. No auth or multi-user deployment. Fonts are packaged through Fontsource, with no runtime Google Fonts request. Production uses the same API and compiled static assets.

sources.title: Ripple verification (document excerpt)
sources.text: - For storage, transaction or engine changes, run `npm run doctor` as well. Use disposable databases. A failed write must preserve item revision, change/review records and evidence together; a successful restart must preserve them together.
